title: Sameer and Anita talk about village and city
body: Sameer lives in a village. One day he meets Anita, who has come from a city to visit her grandparents. Anita tells him that the city is busy, crowded and noisy, with tall buildings everywhere, and that people there are more independent and often do not even know their neighbours. Sameer says that in his village everyone knows everyone else; people work together in the fields, celebrate festivals together and even make decisions as a community. Anita replies that there is still some sense of community in the city: after heavy rains, a house collapsed two streets away, and dozens of people gathered to clear the rubble and make sure no one was trapped. She adds that the city also has local bodies and elected representatives. Sameer explains that his village Panchayat is similar, only smaller; because members know each other, many more people can take part, and even children are sometimes heard. Some children once noticed an electricity wire hanging dangerously low, reported it and explained to a Gram Sabha member that the electric post should be shifted, and it was done. Anita concludes that democracy may seem more complicated in the city, but the idea is the same: everyone's voice matters.
